title: Require explicit human signature to enforce blocking rules
context: Agents could record corrections as human-confirmed even when humans never reviewed them, allowing auto-generated rules to block commits across the repository. This conflated agent-generated advice with human-authorized enforcement, creating accountability gaps.
decision: Decouple reporting from enforcement: corrections land immediately and are surfaced everywhere (reporting tier), but can only block commits after explicit human countersign (enforcement tier). New un-vouched corrections capped at 'warning' authority. Decisions depending on path absence must explicitly anchor where they're searching, so renaming that area is detected as unknown rather than silently continuing under false assumptions.
consequences: Hard-blocking rules require deliberate human action, not agent assertion alone
Audit trail now shows who actually authorized enforcement vs. who just noted it
System fails honestly when context vanishes (renamed paths, deleted anchors) instead of continuing under stale assumptions
Existing records in the graph keep their current authority (no retroactive downgrade of deployed configs)
Agent-generated corrections still provide immediate feedback, just at warning level until confirmed
alternatives_rejected: Prevent agents from generating corrections at all (loses real-time feedback value)
Retroactively weaken all existing rules to warning (breaks existing deployments and user configs)
Allow path_absent without anchor (continues silent failures when code is moved or deleted)
Treat agent signature same as human signature (keeps accountability gap that the change fixes)
